ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 18971, as amended) together with its Enforcement Decree, the Regulation on the Reporting and Use of Financial Transaction Information issued by the Financial Intelligence Unit of Korea (KoFIU), the Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality Act, and the Act on Regulation of Foreign Exchange Transactions, as the governing Korean AML/CFT and UBO identification framework; supervision is exercised by the Financial Services Commission, KoFIU, and the National Tax Service.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registration Office, Court Administration Office of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel mutually exclusive paths: Hague Apostille route = registration extract issued by the commercial registration court, notarization of the issuing officer signature by a Korean notary public, then Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. Consular route for non-Hague states = same extract, notarization, MOFA confirmation, then legalization by the embassy or consulate of the destination jurisdiction. Apostille and consular legalization are never combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Tax and Registration Clearance Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service, District Tax Office with jurisdiction over the registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: certificate obtained from NTS Hometax, notarization by Korean notary if required, Apostille by MOFA. Non-Hague consular path: certificate, notarization, MOFA confirmation, then consular legalization by destination mission. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution Authorizing Formation and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators and anticipated Board of Directors of KR_YUHANGHOESA, notarized by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille Convention states: execution by incorporators/board, Korean notarization, MOFA Apostille. For non-member states: execution, Korean notarization, MOFA confirmation, consular legalization at the destination embassy/consulate. Never chain Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: KR_YUHANGHOESA through its incorporators, certified by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague route: notarized Articles, MOFA Apostille. Consular route: notarized Articles, MOFA confirmation, diplomatic legalization in the destination jurisdiction. These routes are mutually exclusive and run in parallel only as alternatives, never sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Korean commercial bank maintaining the corporate account (e.g., Kookmin Bank, Shinhan Bank, Woori Bank, Hana Bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issued directly by the bank to the requesting party or notarized at the bank with the authorized signatory. If requested by a foreign institution, the bank letter may be notarized and then either apostilled by MOFA (Hague state) or consular legalized (non-Hague state), depending solely on the destination requirement; the two paths are never cumulatively applied.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: KR_YUHANGHOESA must screen every shareholder, direct and intermediate beneficial owner, director, authorized signatory, senior manager, and material counterparty against the KoFIU designated list and Korean Financial Intelligence Unit guidance, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the United States OFAC SDN list, the UK and EU consolidated sanctions lists, and Korean tax and criminal justice alert databases. Screening must cover exact Unicode matches, romanized and transliteration variants, birth date and national identifier matching, and must be repeated at formation, on any ownership change, at each account opening, and then continuously through transaction monitoring. PEP screening must identify foreign and domestic politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates. The CMRA mail-scanning activity is classified as medium-risk enhanced, requiring Enhanced Due Diligence, source-of-funds evidence, UBO re-verification at least annually, and STR filing to KoFIU within three business days for any suspicious activity.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office (IROS) of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea, accessible at https://www.iros.go.kr; commercial name search and clearance are handled through the Commercial Registration Bureau of the district court for the intended registered office.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered corporate name of a Yuhan Hoesa must include the legal form marker Yuhan Hoesa and be entered in Hangul in the Korean commercial register. A foreign-language or romanized name is supplementary and must follow a phonetic Hangul transliteration doctrine. The name clearance doctrine is four-tier: (i) mandatory legal-form indicator, (ii) distinctive main element to avoid identity with existing companies, (iii) business-purpose or descriptive element, and (iv) structural suffix or serial designation. The registry will reject identical or deceptively similar names for entities with the same business purpose within the same registration district.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Commercial Registration Office rejects the chosen name, the applicant must read the rejection notice and immediately prepare a corrected Hangul name that does not conflict with an existing registered entity. Under the Registration of Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act, the applicant may file a written immediate appeal with the district court having jurisdiction over the registration office within 14 days of service, attaching the rejected application, the registry rejection order, a fresh name-search record, corrected Articles of Association, and a counsel opinion. The court will decide whether the name is distinct and lawful. Alternatively, the applicant may withdraw and refile a new reservation to avoid delay, or pursue an administrative appeal if the registry misapplied the Commercial Act. All filing receipts, timestamps and case numbers must be retained for the dossier.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Korean law requires a definite registered address in the Republic of Korea that can receive legal process, court notices, and tax correspondence; a post-office box is not acceptable. For this ISIC 8299 commercial mail receiving and scanning business, a virtual office is conditionally permissible only if the service provider supplies a physical suite with a substantiated lease, a visible company sign, an authorized local agent available during business hours, and an operational mail-scanning service. In practice, the National Tax Service and Korean banks will reject a pure mailbox or forwarding service where no employee is accessible and business records are kept exclusively offshore. The entity must maintain a place of business, lease records, and independently retrievable accounting and AML/CFT data; otherwise the virtual-office model will be disregarded for corporate, tax, and bank-account opening purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) visible name plate at the registered suite, (2) provider permission for unannounced Korean tax or registry inspection, (3) availability of board minutes, register of members, accounting books, VAT records, and mail-scanning logs at the registered office or through electronic access, (4) dedicated work area, telephone line, and authorized agent present, (5) no registered address that is a P.O. Box or private dwelling, (6) business licenses and tax registration displayed, (7) data-protection and AML/CFT policy for mail scanning. Quantified risk: for a low-cost virtual-office CMRA sublease in Seoul or Busan, the estimated likelihood of unannounced National Tax Service on-site inspection under Article 81 of the National Tax Basic Act is high, approximately 60-75 percent within the first 24 months; for a fully leased serviced office with staff, signage, and complete records, the risk declines to approximately 25-40 percent. Municipal district authorities may also perform business-site verification during VAT registration review.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Internet Registration Office (IROS), Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Chapter 4-2 (Yuhan Hoesa), Articles 287-2 through 287-74; Article 34 (incorporation registration); Articles 287-5 and 287-6 (notarization of articles); Article 287-11 (valuation of in-kind contributions); Registration Fees Act and Enforcement Decree.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the Local District Court (Local Court Registry Office) under the Supreme Court Registry Administration of the Republic of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Incorporation and the statutory Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa, together with the Certificate of Deposit of Paid-In Capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Korean Commercial Act sets no minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa. The subscribers may stipulate any positive amount in the Articles; no blocked escrow account is required by Korean law. Cash contributions must be deposited before registration in a domestic bank or postal savings account opened in the name of the company-to-be-formed, and the deposit certificate must be submitted to the registry. Funds may not be withdrawn before registration. Any in-kind contribution must be appraised by a court-appointed examiner and the appraisal report attached to the registration petition.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION IN WRITING OF THE INCORPORATOR AND FIRST MEETING OF DIRECTORS OF YUHANGHOESA, a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) organized under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea.

WHEREAS, the persons whose names appear on the subscribed contribution schedule have agreed to form YUHANGHOESA for the lawful commercial activities set forth in its Articles of Incorporation, including commercial mail receiving, virtual office administration, document scanning, and related business-support services;

WHEREAS, the subscribers have executed and acknowledged the Articles of Incorporation and have caused the same to be authenticated by a duly commissioned notary public as required by Korean law;

WHEREAS, the full subscription amount stated in the Articles has been deposited or, in the case of non-cash contributions, valued and examined in conformity with the Commercial Act;

NOW, THEREFORE, upon due deliberation and with the requisite quorum, it is hereby RESOLVED as follows:

1. Adoption and Ratification of the Articles of Incorporation. The final draft of the Articles of Incorporation presented to this meeting is approved in its entirety and ratified as the foundational corporate charter of the company. The Representative Director is authorized and instructed to submit the Articles and all required annexes to the Local District Court Registry Office and to prosecute the registration to completion.

2. Share Capital and Subscription. The subscribed contribution schedule, showing each member's contribution in cash or in kind and the corresponding percentage of ownership, is adopted. The total paid-up capital shall be fully credited to the company's capital account upon registration. The Representative Director is authorized to release funds held in the temporary deposit account only after the issuance of the certificate of incorporation registration and to treat the released funds as ordinary corporate assets.

3. Banking Authorization. The Representative Director, together with the other director if required by the bank's internal control policy, is authorized to open corporate bank accounts, to execute account agreements, to designate check signatories, to enroll in electronic banking, and to give the bank instructions consistent with this resolution. Any two authorized officers shall execute all documents requiring corporate signature, unless a single signatory is expressly permitted by the bank under written delegation.

4. Registered Office and Service of Process. The registered office identified in the Articles is adopted as the company's legal seat and principal place of business. Company records, corporate seal, and statutory registers shall be maintained at that address, and the Representative Director is directed to notify all governmental authorities, banks, and mail-processing partners of the registered office and any subsequent changes.

5. Appointment and Powers of Statutory Officers. The following persons are appointed to hold office until the next ordinary meeting or until earlier resignation or removal: [INSERT NAME] as Representative Director and [INSERT NAME] as Director. The Representative Director is delegated full authority to negotiate, sign, deliver, and perform all contracts and filings, to apply for tax registrations, licenses, permits, and bank facilities, and to procure professional advice necessary for the company's registered activities.

6. Licenses and Post-Incorporation Actions. The Representative Director and Director are instructed to complete business registration with the National Tax Service, obtain all municipal and industry approvals, register the corporate seal, open the company's active bank account, adopt accounting books, and comply with all applicable anti-money-laundering customer-due-diligence requirements.

7. Ratification and Continuing Effect. Every lawful act performed by the incorporators before the date of this resolution in furtherance of the establishment of the company is ratified. This resolution shall remain in full force and effect until revoked or modified by a subsequent resolution of the members or directors, as applicable under the Commercial Act and the Articles of Incorporation.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the officers are authorized to certify copies of this resolution to banks, tax authorities, and licensing officials as evidence of corporate authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarize and finalize the Articles of Incorporation and subscriber schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Notary Public commissioned under the Notary Public Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation containing the company name, permitted business objects, registered office address, total capital, each subscriber's contribution amount and kind, valuation methods for in-kind property, rules for admission of members, and provisions for appointment and dismissal of directors. All subscribers or their lawfully authorized attorneys-in-fact must sign the Articles personally, and the signatures must be notarized by a Korean notary public. If a subscriber is a foreign national, certified passport copies and, where necessary, an apostilled power of attorney must accompany the notary instruction. The notarized Articles are the master reference for the entire registration.
required_dossiers: Final draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean or bilingual version
Passport or national identity card copy of each subscriber
Certificate of foreign address or Korean Alien Registration Card for non-residents
Power of attorney, if signed by an agent, with notarized/apostilled certification
Business plan or object statement supporting the registered purpose codes
Subscriber contributory schedule showing cash and in-kind valuations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses authentication due to incomplete signatures or unclear object clauses, correct the Articles, obtain the missing subscriber consensus in writing, and re-present the complete package within three business days. Any party objecting to the valuation of in-kind property must be added to the examiner procedure before notarization is completed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit paid-in capital and obtain in-kind contribution appraisal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Domestic commercial bank in Korea and the Local District Court (for appointment of examiner)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital deposit account in the name of YUHANGHOESA at a Korean bank and deposit every cash contribution before the registration application is submitted. Obtain from the bank a written Certificate of Deposit of Paid-In Capital showing the depositor, beneficiary company name, deposit date, and amount. If any subscriber contributes property in lieu of cash, file a petition with the Local District Court for appointment of an independent examiner; the examiner must value the property as of the contribution date and issue a written appraisal report. The report and bank certificate become attachments to the incorporation registration petition and must match Articles values exactly.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Incorporator bank account opening form and anti-money-laundering declaration
Cash deposit receipt or bank certificate of paid-in capital
Court petition form for examiner appointment, if in-kind contribution exists
Valuation report of court-appointed examiner
Statement of account with subscriber names and contribution amounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank withholds the deposit certificate for KYC reasons, submit enhanced due diligence documentation, including source-of-wealth statements and corporate ownership chart, or select an alternative licensed bank. If the court examiner questions in-kind valuation, obtain supplementary appraisals or amend the Articles to reflect a reduced contribution and obtain subscriber consent in writing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File incorporation registration with the Local District Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Court Registry Office (Court of Registration) having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statutory application for registration of incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa. Identify the court having jurisdiction over the location of the company's registered office, usually the district court governing the municipality where the virtual office is physically situated. Submit the notarized Articles, the bank payment certificate, the in-kind appraisal report if any, written consents of the appointed directors, a statement confirming the registered office, and evidence of identity for each representative officer. Pay the court registration fees and local governments registration tax in the amounts calculated by the registry. After substantive review, the registry examiner will enter the company in the commercial register and issue the certificate of incorporation registration.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Application for Registration of Incorporation
Certificate of Deposit of Paid-In Capital
Court examiner's appraisal report, if applicable
Consent-to-act letters signed by each director and representative director
Certified copy of each director's identification or passport
Power of attorney for any local agent handling the filing
Proof of payment of registration tax and court fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a supplementary instruction or a rejection, cure the deficiency by filing the requested document within the stated period, usually two weeks. Where the deficiency relates to valuation or signature authentication, obtain fresh notarization and re-file. If the court refuses registration in whole, the applicant may file a one-week immediate appeal with the reviewing panel of the District Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete national tax business registration and obtain corporate tax identifiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) - Local District Tax Office serving the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the court issues the certificate of incorporation registration, access the online HomeTax portal or appear at the local district tax office and file for a national business registration certificate under the Value-Added Tax Act. State the commencement date of virtual office and mail scanning services and use the Korean industrial classification code corresponding to ISIC 8299 / NAICS 561431. Submit the certificate of incorporation registration, the Articles, the landlord's or virtual office provider's occupancy permission, and identification records. The tax office will issue the Business Registration Certificate, a corporate tax account number, and the VAT registration details. The certificate should be printed and kept at the registered office for bank KYC and licensing procedures.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation registration
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Business registration application form
Lease agreement or virtual office service agreement proving occupancy of the registered office
Representative director's identification and proof of appointment
Corporate seal and seal certificate declaration, where requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office queries the nature of a virtual office business, submit a service explanation letter describing the mail receiving, scanning, forwarding, and document management process, and prove that the registered address is the real operational center for receipt of service of process and records. If the business is not yet active, provide a definitive commencement date and the tax office may issue a pre-commencement registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open corporate bank account, report corporate seal, and onboard governance records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Domestic Korean commercial bank and the local municipal seal registration office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the issued Business Registration Certificate, the certificate of incorporation registration, the notarized Articles, and the board resolution, open the company's operating bank account. The bank will run corporate KYC checks and request beneficial ownership information, especially because commercial mail receiving and document scanning is designated a medium-risk activity under financial action task force-style AML rules. Simultaneously, report the corporate seal to the competent municipality so the bank and outside counsel can obtain official seal certificates. Adopt a statutory register of members, director registers, minute book, accounting books, and an AML/ownership disclosure file. This completes the operational corporate governance layer.
required_dossiers: Business Registration Certificate
Certificate of incorporation registration
Board resolution authorizing bank account opening
Corporate seal and seal registration certificate
Passport and resident registration proof of each authorized officer
Beneficial ownership declaration and source of funds statement
Articles of Incorporation and financial projections if required by the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines the account application because of the medium-risk classification, provide a stronger compliance package: copies of client contracts, data-protection policies, and evidence that the company does not act as a money-services business. If the requested information is rejected, seek onboarding at another bank and simultaneously request the regulator to mediate under the anti-money-laundering supervisory complaints mechanism.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial manufacturing authority is engaged for the specified virtual office and mail scanning services. The licensing authority is the National Tax Service local district tax office for the business registration certificate, and the relevant municipal or provincial licensing office for office occupancy and local permits. If the company receives or forwards physical letters on behalf of third parties as a private mail receiving agency, the post and communications licensing unit of the Ministry of Science and ICT or Korea Communications Commission under the Postal Logistics Act is the competent registrar.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Registration Certificate under the Value-Added Tax Act, together with the required Private Mail Receiving Agency registration under the Postal Logistics Act where physical mail is accepted, stored, scanned, or forwarded as an intermediary. No separate industrial manufacturing or operating license is required because the activity is a non-manufacturing business-support service.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea and Korea Environment Corporation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Not Applicable. The ISIC 8299 virtual office and mail scanning service involves no physical manufacturing, no chemical processing, no assembly line, and no warehousing footprint. Accordingly, no Full Environmental Impact Assessment, Initial Environmental Examination, or Environmental Registration is required. Only ordinary office waste management rules apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - there is no industrial wastewater discharge, no VOC emission source, and no hazardous waste stream. Paper and packaging generated from mail scanning must be recycled or disposed of through licensed municipal waste contractors; any e-waste arising from failed scanning equipment must be handled in accordance with the Promotion of Saving and Recycling of Resources Act rather than through ordinary trash.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for manufacturing or warehousing fire permits. The virtual office, if physically occupied, must comply with the Fire Services Act, including installation of fire extinguishers, smoke detectors, emergency exit signage, and unrestricted egress, with the building owner holding a fire-fighting performance certificate. If the company employs at least one worker in Korea, it must prepare workplace safety and health rules under the Occupational Safety and Health Act and report the establishment to the Ministry of Employment and Labor; no special civil defense shelter approval is required for this non-industrial service occupancy.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, using the HomeTax electronic tax portal (hometax.go.kr); Korea Customs Service is the counterpart authority for export declarations and customs evidence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-invested Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) must first incorporate under the Commercial Act and obtain a Korean registered address. For VAT and direct tax purposes, the representative or a retained resident tax administrator must file a business registration application with the District Tax Office having jurisdiction over the registered office, using the HomeTax portal or in-person. The application is accompanied by the certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, foreign registration certificate of the ultimate parent if any, passport or government-issued ID of the statutory representative, power of attorney, lease evidence of the virtual office, and proof of any required CMRA license or permit. Upon acceptance, National Tax Service issues the 10-digit Korean Business Registration Number, which serves as the TIN and VAT ID. The entity must then obtain a HomeTax electronic certificate (e-cert) for the signatory, register the address and bank accounts in HomeTax, and activate electronic e-tax invoice issuance. If no place of business is maintained in Korea and the non-resident entity is only indirectly present, a non-resident VAT registration can also be pursued through a Domestic Tax Representative under the Framework Act on National Taxes, but the operating Yuhan Hoesa is expected to register directly as a domestic corporation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Yuhan Hoesa is a Korean domestic corporation and is automatically subject to Korean Corporation Tax on its worldwide income at the entity level. There is no pass-through or partnership tax classification for LLC-style limited liability companies in Korea.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not provide a check-the-box election or hybrid mismatch classification election. The entity cannot elect to be disregarded or treated as a transparent partnership. Only separate elective provisions such as the domestic consolidated corporate tax regime for 100% owned subsidiaries exist, and they do not alter the entity's default entity-level classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value Added Tax Act and its Enforcement Decree.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No VAT registration threshold: a business must register from the first taxable supply of goods or services in Korea (KRW 0). A simplified VAT compliance regime applies to certain individual businesses with annual taxable turnover not exceeding KRW 80,000,000, but this is not a registration exemption and does not apply to a corporate Yuhan Hoesa.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All Korean registered businesses must issue electronic tax invoices through the NTS HomeTax system for every B2B supply and zero-rated export supply. The e-tax invoice must be transmitted to HomeTax by no later than the day following the date of issuance; for monthly aggregated invoices, the same one-day post-issuance transmission rule applies. HomeTax validates the taxpayer identification number, invoice sequence, and issue date, and credit-card payments are matched through approved card acquirers. There is no separate physical fiscal stamp or real-time pre-clearance; the post-issuance HomeTax transmission is the anti-fraud control event. Third-party ERP and billing systems must submit via HomeTax EDI or use certified e-cert authentication and cannot alter transmitted invoice data.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for goods physically exported from Korea and for services supplied in connection with export trade or supplied to a non-resident person where the place of supply is outside Korea. For virtual-office, mail-receiving, and digital scanning services, the business must demonstrate that the service recipient is a foreign business or individual located abroad, that the contract and performance evidence identify the service as consumed outside Korea, and that the consideration is paid from abroad. If the service is deemed used in Korea or is supplied to a Korean customer, it is taxable at 10%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service electronic export declaration with the Export Declaration Number and evidence of loading out of Korea
Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill, or another transport document evidencing international movement of goods
Commercial invoice and packing list consistent with the export declaration
Bank-issued Foreign Exchange Acquisition Confirmation (often referred to as an Inward Remittance Certificate) proving receipt of the export proceeds in foreign currency
HomeTax zero-rated electronic tax invoice carrying the export identifier or supporting service export details
For service exports: signed service contract, scope-of-work, output and service delivery logs such as digital mail-scanning records, and proof of the foreign customer's payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS automatically cross-checks Korea Customs Service declarations, HomeTax e-tax invoices, and bank foreign exchange remittance data. If the zero-rating substantiation bundle is incomplete, inconsistent, or fraudulent, the supply is reclassified as domestic taxable, VAT at 10% is assessed, and statutory interest runs from the original due date. The general assessment period is five years, extended to ten years for fraud or intentional concealment. Penalty additions under the Framework Act on National Taxes can range from 10% for a simple understatement to 40% for dishonest or unfair understatement, and failure to issue or late submission of an electronic tax invoice attracts additional tax equal to 1% to 2% of the relevant supply value. Intentional false export invoices or false documentation can result in criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, including imprisonment and fines, plus Customs Act penalties for false declarations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) in conjunction with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South Korean won (KRW) operates under a partially liberalized convertibility regime. Current account transactions are fully convertible and free of quantitative restrictions, while capital account transactions are liberalized but subject to declaration, reporting, or licensing through designated authorized foreign exchange banks. Foreign investors may inject capital into a Korean Yuhan Hoesa without prior approval except for sectors on the negative list, but each inward remittance must be reported under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations and logged in the Foreign Exchange Monitoring System. Export proceeds may be retained in foreign currency accounts, but must be collected within the statutory deadline and reported upon settlement. Profit and dividend remittance to non-resident shareholders is permitted once the entity files corporate tax returns, proves settlement of taxes, and submits audited financial statements along with a Foreign Exchange Declaration at the remitting bank. There is no mandatory conversion of foreign currency export earnings into KRW, but all foreign exchange dealings must be routed through banks licensed by the MOEF, and any deferred collection or non-refund requires documentary justification. Transfer pricing and tax clearance certificates are required before foreign remittance of royalties or service fees. Overall, Korea is an open capital account economy, but the regulatory emphasis is on rigorous record-keeping, real transaction verification, and anti-money laundering vigilance rather than exchange controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and relevant BOK/MOEF notifications, exporters must collect export proceeds within 15 months from the date of export declaration or the contractual payment due date, whichever is earlier. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; exporters are free to retain proceeds in won or foreign currency. However, the exporter must report the receipt of export proceeds to the authorized foreign exchange bank through the settlement system, and any extension beyond the statutory timeline requires prior approval with valid justification. All collection must be evidenced with bank statements, invoices, packing lists, and customs declaration data.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Export Proceeds Collection Account
Foreign Currency Account for Receivables and Disbursements
Virtual Office Mail Scanning Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital electronic money institutions (EMIs) are not licensed as authorized foreign exchange banks under the Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and they cannot provide KRW-denominated account numbers or IBANs for domestic corporate entities. A Korean Yuhan Hoesa must hold its operating bank account at a domestic tier-1 commercial bank. Fintech EMIs may only act as payment acceptance gateways, such as Stripe or PayPal, which route card and recurring subscription proceeds through domestic acquiring banks into a local Korean corporate account. Cross-border settlement with EMIs outside Korea is further constrained by Korean capital movement regulations requiring all foreign exchange transactions to be executed via authorized domestic banks. Therefore, the viable treasury architecture is Stripe for recurring card intake, with settlement falling into an onshore bank account at a tier-1 domestic bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under Korea's Anti-Money Laundering Guidelines and the Act on Prohibition of Financing for Offenses of Public Revenue, all statutory directors and authorized signatories are generally required to appear in person at the bank branch or a diplomatic/consular post abroad when opening a corporate account. While some banks allow remote video KYC for existing customers, initial onboarding of a virtual-office CMRA entity triggers enhanced due diligence, and the final beneficial owner must either physically attend the domestic branch or provide a certified proxy with a notarized, apostilled power of attorney and passport. The bank compliance team will also require a site visit or an independent verification report from a licensed Korean CPA if the entity lacks a physical office address.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Medium-risk commercial mail receiving agency scope (ISIC 8299) combined with 100% non-resident ownership and virtual office registration
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete corporate registration excerpt issued by the Korean court registry, the Yuhan Hoesa's articles of incorporation, a valid virtual office lease agreement, certificate of statutory license for mail scanning operations, notarized identification and apostilled passport for every shareholder and UBO, plus professional reference letters from the incorporator's home-country bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency, low-ticket recurring digital payments via Stripe and credit cards without clear underlying client contracts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Client subscription master agreement, service level mapping of mail scanning and forwarding charges, monthly transactional reconciliation reports, a strong business intelligence dashboard showing the commercial substance of the CMRA, and a documented AML risk assessment showing the entity's client screening and sanctions filtering procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected multiple inbound wires from overseas group companies or shareholders classified as capital injections vs service income
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group treasury and capital structure diagram, electronic board minutes approving investments, executed loan or equity subscription documents, foreign exchange declaration forms with purpose codes, and audited financial statements from the previous period to prove the arm's-length nature of cross-border flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of physical operating site and staff in South Korea triggering shell-company red flag
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A certified registered office agreement, the official virtual office and mail scanning license, an updated business plan, a sworn declaration from the Korean CPA verifying the substance of mail scanning activities, and an undertaking to submit annual corporate filings and audit reports for the first three fiscal years.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contribution for the KR YUHANGHOESA must be wired via SWIFT MT103 to the bank's nostro account with a clear purpose code matching the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS) declaration. For equity capital injection, use purpose code 400000 (capital acquisition by non-residents) and submit the Foreign Exchange Declaration Form to the branch before the funds are credited. The bank will issue a Capital Verification Certificate upon receipt, which must be reviewed by a licensed Korean accountant for entity capital verification. All shareholder remittances must be sourced to bank accounts under the shareholder's name, and rebates or letters of credit discharge must be avoided to prevent suspicion of circular flow. Funds should be held initially in a Capital Escrow Account and then transferred to the operating KRW account once the capital verification is completed and the corporate registry updates are filed.

stage_4.outbound_trade_disbursements: For operational outflows such as software subscriptions, overseas marketing, or supplier payments, the Yuhan Hoesa should use SWIFT MT103 wires with appropriate purpose codes like 100600 (royalty) or 100400 (business service fees) and attach underlying contracts and tax invoices. For high-value physical equipment or inventory procurement, a Commercial Letter of Credit (sight or usance) through the domestic tier-1 bank provides greater security, and Documentary Collections (D/P and D/A) are acceptable for established trading partner relationships. All disbursements above USD 5,000 require a valid foreign exchange declaration and evidence of corporate authorization such as board minutes and signatory matrix. Tax withholding on domestic service portions must be settled through the Hong-Home Tax system before the international wire is released.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore FX forward contracts (KRW/USD, KRW/EUR, KRW/JPY) with a tenure of up to 12 months, provided the underlying exposure from CMRA subscription and operational invoices is fully documented
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) via authorized Korean commercial banks for hedging KRW exposures against offshore settlement, subject to strict documentary proof of underlying non-trade transactions
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for matching a capital injection denominated in USD or EUR converted to KRW for office lease and local OPEX
Plain-vanilla FX options (call or put on KRW) permitted for balance-sheet hedging, with disclosure to the Bank of Korea through the designated foreign exchange bank

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Korean CT-1 and attachments)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the HomeTax portal at the competent district tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of the third month following the close of the taxable year, i.e., 31 March for a calendar-year company; an extension may be permitted by the competent tax office for justifiable circumstances
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment surcharge of 0.022% per day (approximately 8.03% per annum) accrues from the day following the statutory due date; unfaithful or non-filed returns carry a 20% penalty on the underreported or unpaid corporate tax; persistent non-filing after NTS demand triggers seizure of bank accounts and receivables, criminal penalties under the Framework Act on National Taxes, and administrative asset forfeiture; tax delinquency alone does not cause an administrative strike-off of the legal entity under the Commercial Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and approval at the members' meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Members of the Yuhan Hoesa acting as the supreme corporate body; if the company is audited, also the Financial Supervisory Service under external audit rules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after each fiscal-year end, i.e., by 30 June for a calendar-year company; the balance sheet, profit-and-loss statement, and directors' report must be presented for members' approval at the annual meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to obtain member approval within the statutory window are personally liable to the company and creditors for unlawful distributions; repeated breach of the approval duty gives a member standing to petition the district court for dissolution of the Yuhan Hoesa; if the statements are not retained for the prescribed period, criminal fines apply

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External audit report submission to the Financial Supervisory Service, if the audit threshold is met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) via the DART electronic disclosure system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year audited Yuhan Hoesa, the audit report must be filed with the FSS and presented to members within six months after year-end, i.e., by 30 June; public-interest designated companies are subject to the filing deadline of 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit an external audit report is a violation of the Act on External Audit and subjects responsible directors to fines up to KRW 50 million; the FSS may order a corrective audit, reassign the statutory auditor, and refer criminal charges; in serious cases the FSS may bar the company from filing required reports, leading to compulsory audit receivership and forfeiture of tax deductible status

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual compliance report of the commercial mail receiving agency (CMRA) license
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT) acting through Korea Post supervisory authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 January following the prior complete calendar year, unless the license specifies another renewal window; the report must confirm the registered virtual office address, mail scanning procedure, cloud data handling, and enhanced due diligence procedures
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or fraudulent filing permits revocation or forfeiture of the postal agency license; continued unlicensed operation constitutes a criminal offense under the Postal Service Act, and the third-party mail scanning operation may be administratively shut down with forfeiture of deposited postal items

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Zero-value local corporate income tax and local surtax declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Government tax office (Si/Gun/Gu jurisdiction where the registered office is located)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 April following the close of the fiscal year for calendar-year taxpayers, using the same basis period as the national corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid local corporate income tax accrues an additional 0.05% per day penalty; non-filing triggers a tax lien, property seizure, and obligatory compliance order; local tax delinquency cannot independently strike off the Yuhan Hoesa but attracts criminal sanctions under the Local Tax Collection Act

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent CPA audit is required under Article 2 of the Act on External Audit where any of the following is present: (a) total assets at the balance-sheet date equal or exceed KRW 10 billion, approximately USD 7.7 million at an exchange rate of KRW 1,300 per United States dollar; (b) the entity is classified by the Financial Supervisory Service as a public-interest company due to a listing, a financial or payment intermediary license, or annual consolidated revenue above KRW 100 billion; (c) a supervisory ministry or the National Tax Service requires an external audit as a condition of licensure or tax compliance; or (d) at least 50 full-time year-round employees are present together with total assets of KRW 10 billion or more, if the SME exemption otherwise applies. For an ordinary private Yuhan Hoesa engaged primarily in virtual office and mail scanning services that falls below these balance-sheet thresholds, no statutory independent certified audit is legally mandated.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Companies that are subject to statutory audit must apply Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS); a small non-audited Yuhan Hoesa may lawfully apply Korean GAAP for Small and Medium-Sized Entities (SME-K-GAAP). For all corporate income tax filings the accounting records must nevertheless be reconciled with the Corporate Income Tax Act and NTS forms, regardless of whether IFRS or SME-K-GAAP is elected.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no separate one-line annual UBO declaration mandated by the Commercial Act for an unlisted private Yuhan Hoesa. Instead the company must: (1) maintain an up-to-date beneficial ownership and member identification file at the registered office; (2) record any transfer of a membership interest (equity interest) in the Korean Commercial Act sense in the required register within 30 days of the transfer, and file the associated details with the NTS in the next corporate tax return cycle; and (3) at the annual members' meeting, formally confirm that no unreported change in beneficial ownership occurred during the year. Given the medium-risk enhanced AML classification attached to the virtual office/mail scanning service, the company must additionally perform an annual customer-facing beneficial-owner re-verification and preserve the result for production to the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit within 7 days of demand.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Managing Members
Register of Charges, Pledges, and Encumbrances
Minute Book of the members' meeting and board of directors

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 2,500 per year for a compliant Korean registered office, virtual office CMRA reception, mail scanning service, and statutory agent oversight
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 10,000 per engagement for a mandatory K-IFRS independent external audit; USD 1,000 - USD 2,500 for an agreed-upon-procedures or review engagement by a CPA if the company elects voluntary assurance below the statutory threshold

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top marginal Korean Corporate Income Tax rate (progressive: 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200M; 19% over KRW 200M to KRW 20B; 21% over KRW 20B to KRW 300B; 24% over KRW 300B). In addition, a 10% local income tax surcharge is levied on the national corporate income tax, producing a 26.4% combined top marginal burden.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No automatic free-zone, patent-box, or special CMRA tax holiday applies to virtual-office/mail-scanning services. An eligible foreign-invested high-technology business located in a designated Free Economic Zone may receive a 50% to 100% corporate income tax exemption/reduction under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act. Ordinary R&D tax credits may apply to qualifying proprietary software and digital-mail-scanning development, and small or medium enterprise (SME) tax incentives may apply only if revenue remains below the statutory SME threshold. The entity should not assume any preferential rate without a specific advance tax ruling or investment notification approval.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Standard Korean corporate income tax return: 'Corporate Income Tax Report under Article 60 of the Corporate Income Tax Act' (법인세법 제60조; HomeTax national tax return code TJ). Filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal (www.hometax.go.kr).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with semi-annual preliminary/interim corporate income tax payments and quarterly VAT returns; the corporate income tax return itself is filed once per fiscal year).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the due date is March 31 of the following year. A filing extension of up to 3 additional months may be available if foreign operations, accounting closing delays, or natural disasters prevent timely filing, subject to National Tax Service approval.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Supporting schedule - International Business Transactions Report (국제거래명세서)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose all cross-border related-party transactions, including their amounts, contractual terms, and the transfer-pricing method applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the total amount of international related-party transactions exceeds the statutory disclosure threshold generally set at KRW 5 billion, file the International Business Transactions Report with the corporate income tax return; Local File and Master File submission obligations generally arise at KRW 10 billion in controlled cross-border transactions and, for Master File, also require group revenue of at least KRW 100 billion. Denominate amounts in KRW; provide contemporaneous economic evidence supporting CUP, resale price, cost plus, TNMM, or profit split. Insufficient documentation permits tax reassessment plus a negligence penalty and additional tax interest.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing with no return: 20% of the unpaid tax under the Framework Act on National Taxes (FANT) Article 47-2. Negligent under-reporting: 10% of the understated tax; fraudulent understatement: 20%. Over-deductions or overstated loss carryforwards trigger an additional 10% to 20% assessment. Late payment interest accrues daily at 0.022% (approximately 8.03% per annum) on unpaid national tax, with a 10% local income tax surcharge on the related national penalties. Criminal tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act can result in imprisonment up to 3 years and a fine up to 3 times the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate withholding (20% national corporate income tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge) on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders who do not have a Korean permanent establishment; the rate may be reduced under an applicable double tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the Korean withholding agent must file the 'Application for Non-Resident Withholding Tax Exemption/Reduction' with the local tax office before remittance, or the non-resident shareholder must file a refund claim within the statutory limitations period (generally 3 years). Mandatory evidence includes: (1) a current Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's country of tax residence; (2) a beneficial ownership declaration confirming the shareholder is the actual economic owner and not a back-to-back conduit; (3) substance records proving the recipient has the capacity to own, manage, and bear risk; and (4) compliance with any Limitation on Benefits clause in the treaty. The Korean National Tax Service may deny relief where the principal purpose is treaty shopping, and the withholding agent then becomes liable for the under-withheld amount plus penalties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory aggregate withholding rate on cross-border interest and royalties is 22% (20% national tax plus 2% local surcharge). Under many Korean DTAs, interest is reduced to 10% to 15%, and royalties are typically reduced to 10% to 15% depending on the treaty and whether the recipient is a related enterprise; certain government/public interest may be exempt. All reduced rates require TRC, beneficial ownership, and economic substance documentation at the time of withholding or through a timely refund claim.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10,000,000,000 (KRW 10 billion) in international related-party transactions generally triggers mandatory Local File and Master File preparation for the fiscal year; the annual International Business Transactions Report and attached financial schedules are required when cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 5,000,000,000. The Master File also applies when the multinational group has consolidated global revenue of at least KRW 100 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea applies an economic substance doctrine through the general anti-abuse rule (Framework Act on National Taxes Article 17), the International Tax Adjustment Act Article 3-2, the controlled foreign company regime, and substantive judicial substance-over-form precedent. A virtual-office and mail-scanning company must demonstrate that its core income-generating activities (CIGA) — client contracting, subscription billing, digital scanning, data storage, cybersecurity, and risk management — are actually performed in Korea using local employees, physical or cloud infrastructure, and Korean bank accounts. A pure mailbox or nominal office with no local activity, no decision-making, and no technical capacity can be disregarded or recharacterized as a conduit; treaty benefits and reduced withholding rates may be denied, and income may be reattributed to the foreign principal.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Tax Evasion and Transactional Shell Schemes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Yuhan Hoesa records recurring 'management fees' and 'mail-scanning subcontract fees' payable to a Hong Kong or British Virgin Islands affiliate that performs no actual services, while distributing remaining cash to non-resident shareholders as 'cost reimbursements', thereby avoiding the 22% dividend withholding tax and artificially reducing Korean taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act Article 3, tax evasion is punishable by imprisonment up to 3 years and a fine up to 3 times the tax evaded. Under FANT Article 47-2, an unfaithful understatement penalty of 20% to 40% plus late-payment interest of 0.022% per day is assessed. Under the International Tax Adjustment Act, transfer-pricing adjustments may add 10% to 30% of the adjusted tax amount for failure to produce contemporaneous documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean Commercial Act Article 401 permits piercing the corporate veil where directors acted with intent or gross negligence. Directors are jointly and severally liable for corporate tax, penalties, and interest; personal bank accounts and assets may be seized; the National Tax Service may impose travel bans and immigration blacklisting; and a criminal conviction carries imprisonment up to 3 years and disqualification from corporate management.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Economic Substance Failure and DTA Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean entity is operated as a nominee-registered virtual office with no local employee, no physical mail-scanning facility, no independent bank account, and no substantive decision-making; the foreign parent uses it solely to invoice Korean merchants and pays out profits as 'royalties' to a low-tax jurisdiction while claiming treaty benefits in the shareholder's residence country to avoid Korean withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service will apply FANT Article 17 and the International Tax Adjustment Act Article 3-2 to deny treaty benefits, recharacterize royalty payments as constructive dividends or Korean-source business income, impose 22% withholding plus local surcharge, and levy unfaithful-report penalties. Repeated use of a shell entity to evade Korean tax is subject to criminal sanctions under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, and the Korean tax authority may cancel the entity's business registration and invalidate its postal/CMRA license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly control the sham structure are personally liable for unreported withholding taxes and penalties under Commercial Act Article 401 and the National Tax Collection Act. Officials may be blacklisted from future government procurement, have Korean business licenses revoked, be subject to travel restrictions, and be criminally prosecuted with imprisonment up to 3 years. Civil restitution extends to the director's personal assets where the tax was collected from customers but intentionally not remitted.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CMRA Regulatory Violation and Unlicensed Mail Forwarding
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The LLC acts as a Commercial Mail Receiving Agency (CMRA) without obtaining the required statutory postal-logistics license, fails to perform customer due diligence or beneficial ownership identification for foreign clients, and processes mail and subscription payments for opaque offshore entities, facilitating money laundering and tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Korea's Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information, failing to file suspicious transaction reports can be punished by imprisonment up to 3 years and a fine up to KRW 100 million. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, unregistered or falsely reported cross-border remittances are subject to fines of up to 20% of the unreported amount and imprisonment up to 3 years. Under the Postal Logistics Act, operating an unlicensed mail-receiving agency triggers administrative shutdown orders, business registration cancellation, and criminal fines; the Financial Intelligence Unit may add the entity to a high-risk blacklist.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who personally control the unlicensed operation lose limited liability protection and may be held jointly and severally liable for fines, tax deficiencies, and restitution. Directors may face travel bans, asset freezes, criminal imprisonment up to 3 years for AML violations, and disqualification from serving as directors of any Korean corporation. Each director who knowingly enables the scheme can be charged as a co-principal under Korean criminal law.
